record.original_question: Let H be the space of entire maps from C to C or to P1 with the compact-open topology, and let U be the subset of maps h such that translates h(z+a_n) can approximate every f in H. What is the minimal possible growth of the Nevanlinna characteristic Th(r) = ∫_0^r (dt/t) ∫_{D(t)} h^*(ω) for maps h in U?

evidence.quote: Let H denote the space of entire maps from C to C (resp. to P1), endowed with the topology of uniform convergence on compact sets. Let U be the set of h ∈ H such that for any other function f ∈ H, there is a sequence an ∈ C such that han(z) := h(z + an) converges to f.
Problem 9.1. Find the minimal growth of the Nevanlinna characteristic function Th for h ∈ U , where Th(r) := ∫r0 dt/t ∫D(t) h∗(ω) and ω is the Fubini-Study form on P1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{H}$ denote either the space of entire functions $h:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ or the space of holomorphic maps $h:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$, equipped with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$. For $a\in\mathbb{C}$ and $h\in\mathcal{H}$, let $h_a(z):=h(z+a)$ denote the translate of $h$ by $a$. Define $\mathcal{U}\subset\mathcal{H}$ to be the set of maps $h\in\mathcal{H}$ such that the translation orbit $\{h_a : a\in\mathbb{C}\}$ is dense in $\mathcal{H}$; equivalently, for every $f\in\mathcal{H}$ there exists a sequence $(a_n)\subset\mathbb{C}$ with $h_{a_n}\to f$ uniformly on compact subsets of $\mathbb{C}$.

For $h\in\mathcal{H}$ (in the projective case), let $\omega$ denote the Fubini–Study Kähler form on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ (normalized so that $\int_{\mathbb{P}^1}\omega=1$), and define the Nevanlinna (Ahlfors–Shimizu) characteristic
$$T_h(r) := \int_0^r \frac{dt}{t}\int_{D(t)} h^{*}\omega, \qquad r>0,$$
where $D(t)=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<t\}$. (In the entire case, replace $\omega$ by the pullback of the Fubini–Study form under $\mathbb{C}\hookrightarrow\mathbb{P}^1$.)

Determine the minimal possible growth rate of $T_h(r)$ as $r\to\infty$ over all $h\in\mathcal{U}$. More precisely, characterize the infimum, in the sense of growth orders, of the family $\{T_h : h\in\mathcal{U}\}$, and decide whether for every transcendental increasing function $\varphi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ there exists $h\in\mathcal{U}$ with $T_h(r)=O(\varphi(r))$ as $r\to\infty$.
artifact.category_tag: Nevanlinna theory and universal entire functions
artifact.status_search_result: A 2023 preprint constructs universal entire curves in projective spaces whose Nevanlinna characteristic grows slower than any preassigned transcendental growth rate, addressing the projective ($\mathbb{P}^1$) version of the question. This shows there is no transcendental lower bound on the growth, but a precise sharp characterization (and the entire-target case) does not appear to be fully settled.

status_evidence.title: Universal Entire Curves in Projective Spaces with Slow Growth
status_evidence.snippet: We construct explicit universal entire curves in projective spaces whose Nevanlinna characteristic functions grow slower than any preassigned transcendental growth rate.
status_evidence.claim: Universal entire curves into projective space exist with arbitrarily slow (sub-transcendental) Nevanlinna characteristic growth, addressing the minimal-growth question for maps to P^1.

status_evidence.title: Frequently Hypercyclic Meromorphic Curves with Slow Growth
status_evidence.snippet: Hypercyclic entire functions can maintain minimal growth rates; frequent hypercyclicity under slow growth concentrates along countable direction sets.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work continues to refine slow-growth constructions for universal/hypercyclic meromorphic curves, indicating the minimal-growth problem is actively studied and only partially resolved.
